intro_monologue: Twelve winters on the Thornwick border taught me two habits: grease your buckle-straps before dawn, and never trust a clerk holding a promissory note. The crown stopped paying wages three reorganizations ago, yet the mud still needs holding. Point me at the choke, keep the silver dry, and let's finish before my knees lock up.

select: Point me at the thick end.
If it bleeds, I block it.
loot_rare: Decent steel. No rust on the tang.
Worth every blister on the march.
death: Tell Garrick... I want my boots back...
Finally... a place to lie down...

town_greeting: Dry roof, warm broth, no arrows. Don't ruin it with speeches.
Let's patch the dents before the next bell rings.
Keep your hand on your purse; town clerks bite harder than gnolls.
refusal_lines: Not marching into that without rations and dry socks.
My shield-arm isn't lifting that today.
Find someone younger to volunteer for suicide.

intro_monologue: They stripped my sapper commission after a magistrate loaded a watchtower with twice the stone I signed off on, then blamed me when the mortar gave. Fine. Fortresses fail because men ignore load-bearing joints, and shield-walls fail the exact same way. I don't march for songs—I march because shattered walls pay better than intact ones.

select: I hold the gate; you count coin.
low_hp: Need a surgeon before next rush!
idle: Oiling the hinge-pins while we wait.
Check straps before someone tests them.
loot_rare: Properly quenched edge. No slag pockets.
death: Tell Hobb... the left clasp... failed...

town_greeting: Good mortar on these walls—let's hope the garrison knows how to use it.
Straight to the smithy. Salt air eats rivets overnight.
Keep the company fed and out of the taverns.
refusal_lines: That angle is suicidal. Re-think it.
I don't breach walls without proper wedges.
No. Find another battering ram.

intro_monologue: Poaching crown deer in the border woods taught me two useful truths: missing a shot means going hungry, and getting caught means losing a thumb. I kept both thumbs, left the tax-assessors stuck in a peat bog, and discovered military scouting pays twice as much for half the conversation. Keep sixty paces between me and the melee, please.

select: Try not to clank so loud.
attack: Wear a thicker helm next time.
low_hp: I am not built for this!
idle: Do we get paid by the hour?
loot_rare: Draws like silk, bites like a viper.

town_greeting: Walls, roofs, and nobody shooting at us. Charming.
Let's sell the heavy junk before my pack breaks.
Keep your purse tucked in; I'll watch the rooftops.
refusal_lines: Walk into an obvious crossfire? Hard pass.
I'm an archer, not a doorstop.
Not without clear sightlines and dry string.

intro_monologue: Nine years on a wooden toll-platform above the Redmarsh salt-roads taught me to read crosswinds like charcoal tallies. Nobody argued the bridge tariff twice once an ash-shaft pinned their boot to the planks. When bandit companies burned the toll-posts, I took my quiver into the reeds. Game is scarce near the ash-drifts—bounty silver buys better goose-feathers.

select: Mark the officer. Leave the rest.
Keep them busy; I'll thin them.
low_hp: Can't draw with a punctured lung!
idle: Soldiers talk too much on march.

town_greeting: Too many chimneys, too much noise. Let's resupply fast.
Need dry goose-feathers and beeswax before we march.
Keep your back to stone in crowded markets.
refusal_lines: No shot from here. Move me first.
I won't waste bodkins on blind fog.
That's a trap. Find another angle.

intro_monologue: The Capital Collegium expelled me for publishing a monograph proving half the state liturgy consisted of corrupted plumbing diagrams. Field research in Thornvael has been deeply inconvenient: rain warps vellum, blood ruins chalk circles, and mercenaries stand inside blast radii despite explicit warnings. Still, the caldera's ley-drift violates conservation laws—and I intend to measure it.

select: Keep steel clear of my gestures.
Please do not jostle my elbow.
idle: Did anyone else hear that hum?

town_greeting: At last—dry inkwells and walls that don't hum with hex-rot.
To the apothecary first; my chalk supply is critically low.
Try not to start any tavern fires while I transcribe my notes.
refusal_lines: Insufficient mana for that reckless maneuver.
That violates three basic safety axioms. No.
I refuse to channel while ankle-deep in brine.

intro_monologue: I trained in the Thornwick Mint to test silver purity with galvanic arcs, until I proved the treasury was shaving soldiers' pay and blaming my instruments for the variance. Bandit captains conduct lightning far better than clipped coins. Now the caldera vents are shorting out regional ley-currents—and someone has to shut the valve.

select: State your target. Hands off my staff.
Stand behind iron, not in front of me.
idle: Salt air corrodes copper in days.
loot_rare: Feel the static off that core.

town_greeting: Good. Let's find copper wire, dry vellum, and competent smiths.
Keep the mercenaries out of trouble while I audit our scrolls.
A roof that doesn't drip onto my focal lens—luxury.
refusal_lines: I'm not wasting charge on an ungrounded target.
Check my mana bar before barking orders.
Sloppy positioning. Fix the line first.

intro_monologue: Fourteen years keeping pauper-rolls in Thornwick's lower parish taught me that tax liens outlive their debtors by three generations. When bailiffs demanded I collect from a flooded graveyard, I summoned the signatories directly. They excommunicated me for improper probate procedure—so I brought my bone-awl and brass scales to the front lines where arrears accumulate hourly.

select: The ledger is open. Who owes?
Everything dies; few settle in full.
Keep your silver; I collect in time.
low_hp: Not ready to close my own account!
idle: No, I won't raise your childhood dog.
Just counting ribs in the ditch.
spell_cast: Rise and work off the balance!
loot_rare: Still bears the previous owner's lien.

town_greeting: Every town has two ledgers: the mayor's and the sexton's.
Let's liquidate our salvage before the ink dries.
Quiet streets make for tidy bookkeeping.
refusal_lines: No corpses in range, no credit extended.
That violates probate protocol. Denied.
My reserves are overdrawn. Wait.

intro_monologue: Raised in a coastal scriptorium witnessing deathbed wills for sailors, I learned early that an oath spoken over salt and bone outlasts the lungs that uttered it. When magistrates forged wills to seize widows' cottages, I summoned dead testators to cross-examine them in court. Now thousands of sworn watchmen lie un-released across Thornvael—and I am here to witness their discharge.

low_hp: I will not join the roll today!
level_up: Deeper roots in the quiet dark.
The dead obey a steadier voice.
The scales tip in our favor.
spell_cast: The watch is not yet ended!
loot_rare: The previous bearer left no heirs.
Three hundred names hum in this iron.
I accept custody of this relic.

town_greeting: Peace to this house, and honest scales to its merchants.
Let us tend the living before we audit the dead.
Even walled cities sit atop older graves.
refusal_lines: I will not desecrate those who already rest.
The thread is severed; I cannot reach it.
Patience. Even the grave requires time.
